transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’ve been getting kind of stuck on how my face looks. We put in a brighter bathroom mirror, and since then I keep noticing the skin around my cheeks and jaw looks uneven, maybe a little saggy. My husband says he doesn’t really see it, but… I do.
How much does thinking about your face affect your daily life?

It’s… not ruining everything, I guess. I still get my work done. But I do spend too long getting ready, and then I’m rushing into the courthouse some mornings. I’ve missed the start of yoga a few times.

And, um… I’ve avoided being in a few casual photos, like at book club or community things. I just didn’t want to think about how my face would look.
Do you find yourself constantly thinking about your face throughout the day?

Not constantly, exactly… but it does come up a lot. Mostly since we put in that brighter mirror, I keep noticing my cheeks and jaw, like the skin looks uneven or kind of saggy. My husband says he doesn’t really see it, but I still notice it.
How upset do you feel when you think about the unevenness or sagging of the skin on your face?

It bothers me… more than I’d like to admit, I guess. When I catch it in that bright mirror, the skin around my cheeks and jaw just looks uneven or saggy to me, and I get stuck on it. My husband says he can’t really see it, but I still feel upset when I notice it.
Has your concern about your face affected your relationships with friends or family?

A little, I guess. I’ve skipped out on a few casual photos at book club and some community events because I didn’t want to deal with worrying about how my face would look.

It hasn’t really stopped me from seeing people, though. I still go. It’s more… I just try to avoid the picture part.
Is it always the same areas of your face, like your cheeks and jaw, that you notice and get stuck on?

Yeah… mostly the same spots. It’s the skin around my cheeks and jaw that I keep noticing, especially in that brighter bathroom mirror. It just looks uneven or kind of saggy to me, even though my husband says he doesn’t really see it.
Do you think your face would look normal if the skin around your cheeks and jaw were perfectly even and not saggy?

I guess… yes, that’s what I keep thinking. Like if that skin around my cheeks and jaw didn’t look so uneven or saggy to me, then maybe my face would just look normal. My husband says he can’t really see it, but since we got that brighter mirror, I notice it all the time.
Do you think you would stop worrying about your face if the skin around your cheeks and jaw looked perfectly even and not saggy to you?

I think so… or at least I’d worry less. It’s really that area—the cheeks and jaw—that I keep seeing in the brighter mirror. If it didn’t look uneven or saggy to me, I don’t think I’d be so stuck on it.
Do you think there's anything else about your appearance that bothers you, or is it mainly the skin around your cheeks and jaw?

It’s mainly that, I think… the skin around my cheeks and jaw. Since we put in that brighter bathroom mirror, I just keep noticing it looking uneven or sort of saggy, even though my husband says he doesn’t really see it.
Do you think you would still notice the unevenness or sagging if you weren't looking in the brighter mirror?

I don’t know… maybe not as much. It really started after we put in that brighter bathroom mirror. That’s where I keep seeing the skin around my cheeks and jaw looking uneven or kind of saggy, even though my husband says he can’t really see it.
Do you think you would worry about your face if you couldn't see yourself in mirrors or reflections?

Probably not as much… I mean, it’s really when I see myself in that brighter bathroom mirror that I start noticing my cheeks and jaw looking uneven or saggy. My husband says he doesn’t really see it, but once I see it, I keep thinking about it.
Has your concern about your face caused you any significant problems at work or in other areas of your life beyond just being late to yoga or avoiding photos?

Not really… I mean, I still get my work done. It’s more that I’ve had to rush into the courthouse a few mornings because I spent too long getting ready. And I’ve missed the start of yoga more than once.

I guess I’ve also avoided being in a few casual photos, like at book club or community events, because I didn’t want to be worrying about how my face looked.
Has your concern about your face caused you significant distress or interfered with your ability to function in daily life in any major way?

Not in a major way, I don’t think. I still do my work. It’s just… I’ve rushed into the courthouse a few mornings because I spent too long getting ready, and I’ve missed the start of yoga more than once. And I’ve skipped a few casual photos at book club or community things because I didn’t want to worry about how my face would look.
Is there something specific about the unevenness or sagging of your skin that bothers you the most?
I guess it’s mostly around my cheeks and jaw. In that brighter mirror, it just looks uneven to me… kind of saggy, like one side doesn’t sit right. My husband says he doesn’t really see it, but I do.
Is it the appearance of the skin around your cheeks and jaw itself that bothers you, or is it more about how you think others might see you because of it?

It’s mostly the way it looks to me, I think. Since we put in that brighter bathroom mirror, I keep noticing the skin around my cheeks and jaw looking uneven… kind of saggy. My husband says he can’t really see it, but I can.
Do you worry that other people are noticing the unevenness or sagging of the skin around your cheeks and jaw when they look at you?

A little, maybe. I mean… it started with me seeing it in that brighter mirror, the cheeks and jaw looking uneven or sort of saggy. My husband says he doesn’t really notice it, so I’m not sure other people do either, but I do worry about it sometimes.
Do you think others can see the unevenness or sagging of the skin around your cheeks and jaw when they look at you?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I can see it, especially in that brighter bathroom mirror… around my cheeks and jaw. But my husband says he can’t really tell what I’m talking about, so maybe other people don’t see it the way I do.
Do you believe that if others could see your face the way you see it, they would also be bothered by the unevenness or sagging of the skin around your cheeks and jaw?

I guess… yes, maybe. If they saw it the way I do in that brighter mirror, the unevenness around my cheeks and jaw, I think they’d probably notice it too. My husband says he doesn’t really see it, though, so I don’t know.
Do you think the unevenness or sagging of the skin around your cheeks and jaw is something that only you can see?

I don’t know if it’s only me. I mean, I keep seeing it since we got that brighter bathroom mirror—the skin around my cheeks and jaw looks uneven, kind of saggy. But my husband says he really can’t see what I’m talking about, so… maybe it is mostly me.
